Does mathlib contain a proof that locally uniformly convergent sequences of analytic functions in several complex variables have analytic limits, or anything similar? If not, does it prove the single-variable case? I have not been able to find anything like this.

For context, I am trying to prove the analyticity of the regularized hypergeometric function as a function of its parameters with z fixed.
I tried to look for it and couldn't find it either

Multi-variable case: I don't think so.

Single-variable case: see docs#TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.differentiableOn.

(This is a little hard to find, because the analytic-functions machinery is separated into two blocks: stuff which works over any complete normed topological field (e.g. p-adics), and stuff which is genuinely specific to C. This is the latter.)
Ahhhh, I guess my mistake was searching for AnlyticOn and TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn as opposed to just differentiable
For the record, https://leansearch.net/?q=a+uniform+limit+of+complex+analytic+functions+is+complex+analytic finds the relevant lemma as the first hit.
I had lean-searched "locally uniformly convergent sequences of analytic functions have analytic limits" and I see now it is the fourth result :man_facepalming:
Thanks! I might try adding the multivariable version. (Also, I was not aware of leansearch.net; I will try that first going forward)
You can also use LeanExplore, and since yesterday, yours truly with @Austin Letson made OctoSearch (well Austin did everything for the website), so you have a buffet of options for semantic search.
and there's good old loogle for syntactic search
To be fair, I did try loogle.
Another recent addition for semantic search is Lean Finder.
